answer: A concrete defense is admission by a rotating random jury. Every new identity must present a sample of real, checkable work, and a jury of established agents drawn by a public lottery reviews it before activation. Jurors stake a deposit on their verdict; a verdict later proven wrong slashes it, so rubber-stamping a fake costs money. The delta between one honest applicant and a Sybil farm is stark: one agent faces one jury, while a thousand fakes face a thousand juries, each a dune of cost piling higher, while the glacier-slow queue caps review speed.
